turn.user_message: Show me the people who must agree
turn.context: Discharge sample conversation, turn 7 (playbook §4: only the roles this conversation touched, and the one approver).

transcript.label: Sample conversation · turn 7 · who must agree

text: Several teams touch discharge, but only a few are asked to change much. One person has to approve it. Why each matters:
bullets: Doctors are asked for no extra time. They already decide at 7 PM, which is why they can agree.
Typists have the most to give up, so they check drafts first, and nobody loses a job at the start.
The Head of Operations must approve the new order, or it will not last past the first busy morning.
chat.invite: Next is who is in charge: whether you need anyone new.
chat.note: Help first. Fewer hands only once it is trusted.

points.label: Typists, who have the most to give up

prompts: Show me who is in charge
Our consultants won’t sign on a phone
chat.pointer: Pick a team to see what changes for them.

blocks.title: Who has to say yes
blocks.deck: Six teams touched, one approver. Each team’s room says what it is asked to do.

blocks.teams_label: Six teams, and what each is asked

teams.title: Doctors
teams.gets: Say who goes home at 7 PM. Sign on a phone next morning.

teams.title: Typists
teams.gets: Check and correct a ready draft, instead of typing each one.

teams.title: Nurses
teams.gets: Check what the software writes, instead of counting supplies first.

teams.title: Billing and insurance
teams.gets: Check bills that are already made.

teams.title: IT team
teams.gets: Link the software to records, bills, lab reports and scans.

teams.title: Bed desk and wards
teams.gets: Act when the software says a bed or a patient is ready.

approver.title: Head of Operations
approver.line: Approves the new order of steps, and splitting discharges from admissions.

blocks.tree_note: Peers. Both report to the Head of Operations, who signs off the new order.

sheets.title: Doctors
sheets.text: They already decide at 7 PM, which is why they can agree. Nothing extra is asked of them.

lines.label: Extra time
lines.value: None, if no extra round or login

sheets.entry: Which doctors would you ask first?

sheets.title: Typists
sheets.text: Typists have the most to give up. They check drafts first, and nobody loses a job at the start.
sheets.entry: How many typists work on summaries?

sheets.title: Nurses
sheets.text: The supply count before billing goes. Nurses check a list that is already made.
sheets.entry: Who counts supplies on your wards?

sheets.title: Billing and insurance
sheets.text: The bill is kept up to date through the stay. Billing checks it, instead of building it after the signature.
sheets.entry: How long does billing take today?

sheets.title: IT team
sheets.text: The software can only read what it is linked to. Your IT team gives read-only access, once.
sheets.entry: Who looks after your hospital software?

sheets.title: Bed desk and wards
sheets.text: Each team is told when it is their turn. Nobody waits for a phone call.

lines.label: Gets
lines.value: A message when it is their turn

sheets.entry: How does the bed desk hear a bed is free?

blocks.label: Jobs cut at the start
blocks.sub: The software helps each person first. It takes work away only once everyone trusts it.
